doc.title: Steve Wilson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 25, 2002

title: Childhood music at home and the Hampton Jazz Festival
summary: Wilson was inspired by his father's records and by festivals in Hampton; his father sang in a choir but did not play.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: That’s a good question. You know I think it was just being inspired very young, being exposed to the music by my father, who is a music enthusiast and had all kinds of music around the house. The first record I remember hearing live was Ahmad Jamal “Live at the Pershing” and of course with “Poinciana” and Miles Davis “Live in Europe.” But there were other things, you know Miriam Makeba, James Brown, he was a big Mario Lanza fan, so there was a whole array of music, and seeing music live when I was small in Hampton, Virginia at the Hampton Jazz Festival, and seeing people like Cannonball Adderley, Eddie Harris, Les McCann, Rahsaan Roland Kirk. Getting all of that early is what inspired me to do it. So I pretty much knew by the time I was twelve or thirteen, this is something I really loved and wanted to do it.
Did your father play an instrument?

No. He sang in a spiritual choir, but not a trained musician. I did have other relatives who were musicians and all of my friends in the neighborhood played music so with all of that it inspired me to do it.
